# Lesson 13 · Working in Visual Studio

> A companion for teams that live in the IDE — Community, Professional and Enterprise compared without prices, the files Visual Studio reads (.vsconfig, .slnx, launchSettings, .runsettings, .editorconfig), the debugger and Test Explorer, and where VS Code and Rider fit

📄 **Lesson PDF:** [lesson-13-visual-studio-workflows.pdf](./lesson-13-visual-studio-workflows.pdf)

## You will be able to

- Explain why dotnet build and Build-in-Visual-Studio give the same result, and name the few things that legitimately differ (workloads, installed SDKs, two command-line-only files)
- Choose between Community, Professional and Enterprise from the licence rules and the features that are gated, using only claims you can check on an official page
- Share a Visual Studio setup through .vsconfig, .slnx, .editorconfig and .runsettings so the IDE and the CLI read the same files
- Drive the debugger with intent: conditional and dependent breakpoints, tracepoints, DebuggerDisplay, exception settings, Just My Code, Hot Reload and its limits
- Run and organise tests in Test Explorer, and reach the same tests, filters and settings from the CLI
- Decide when VS Code with the C# Dev Kit or JetBrains Rider is the better tool for a developer

## Maps from your stack

IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio (Gradle run configurations, the debugger, inspections), VS Code for TypeScript and Python, and the CI pipelines you already run from the command line.
